name: solstice

attributes.attribute: the year's longest day on June 21 and longest night on December 21
the word means the sun sitting still
did not mark the solstices as feasts but knew how to calculate them

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The solstice is a calendar feast. The word means sun sitting still. The sun does appear to stand still in the days around the solstices. The summer solstice falls on June 21, and the winter one on December 21. These are the year's longest day and longest night. On those days the change in the length of the daylight and the night slows. It becomes almost impossible to measure, then begins again as the solstice period ends. The Celts did not remember the solstices as feasts. Yet they must have known how to calculate them. Their own yearly feasts drew on this knowledge. The sun and the turning of the year gave shape to the season, and the solstice marked the hinge of the light and the dark.
